The figure above shows the graph of a piecewise linear function $y=f(x).$ The point $A$ has coordinates $(3,3)$ and lies on $y=f(x).$ Given that $(3,3)$ lies on $y={f}^{-1}(x),$ what is $({f}^{-1})^{′}(3)?$
question.worked_solution:
Since $(3,3)$ lies on ${f}^{-1},$ we have ${f}^{-1}(3)=3.$
The slope of the tangent to $f(x)$ for $x\in [0,6]$ is $\frac{1}{3}$, hence, ${f}^{′}(3)=\frac{1}{3}.$

The formula for the derivative of the inverse function is

$$
({f}^{-1})^{′}(x)=\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(x))}.
$$

Evaluating at $x=3,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}({f}^{-1})^{′}(3) & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(3))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}(3)} \\  & =\frac{1}{(\frac{1}{3})} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$
